topics.name: Mid-latitude cyclones (frontal depression, extra tropical cyclones)
subtopics: Consolidation of Grade 11 global air circulation
General characteristics; areas of formation; conditions necessary for formation
Stages of development; cross-section; weather of cold, warm and occluded fronts
Impact on human activities and the environment; precautionary and management strategies
Synoptic maps and satellite images: stages of development, influence of the South Indian and South Atlantic highs, weather symbols and prediction
Mapwork/GIS: alphanumeric and grid references; coordinates and fixing position

topics.name: Tropical cyclones
subtopics: General characteristics; areas of formation and regional names; formation factors; stages of development
Associated weather patterns; cross-section interpretation
Impact on the environment and human activities; precautionary and management strategies
Identification on synoptic maps and satellite images; case study of ONE recent tropical cyclone affecting southern Africa
Mapwork/GIS: contours and height, compass direction, true bearing; satellite imagery and resolution

topics.name: Subtropical anticyclones and associated weather conditions
subtopics: The three high-pressure cells affecting SA: South Atlantic, South Indian, Kalahari — location, identification, characteristics
Influence of anticyclones on SA weather and climate (plateau, inversion layer, ocean currents, ridging), summer and winter positions
Travelling/moving disturbances: moisture front and line thunderstorms, coastal low pressure, SA berg winds; resultant weather and impact-reduction strategies
Reading anticyclonic circulation and disturbances on synoptic maps and satellite images
Mapwork/GIS: magnetic declination and bearing; comparing map scales; data layering and buffering

topics.name: Valley climates
subtopics: Slope aspect: definition; effect on temperature distribution in a valley
Anabatic and katabatic winds, inversions, thermal belt, frost pockets, radiation fog
Influence on human activities: settlement and farming

topics.name: Urban climates
subtopics: Reasons for differences between rural and urban climates
Urban heat islands: definition, causes, effects, reduction strategies
Pollution domes: definition, causes, effects, reduction strategies

topics.name: Fluvial processes
subtopics: River rejuvenation: definition, reasons, features (knickpoint, terraces, valley-in-a-valley, incised/entrenched meanders), significance
River capture (stream piracy): concepts, features (captor, captured and misfit streams, elbow of capture, wind gap), impacts and implications for human activity
Mapwork: identifying river-capture features; calculating gradient

topics.name: Fluvial processes & catchment and river management
subtopics: Superimposed and antecedent drainage patterns
River management: causes of poor management; importance of drainage basins and catchment areas
Human impact: river pollution (eutrophication), overgrazing, deforestation, settlement
Management strategies; case study of one SA catchment management strategy
GIS: data standardisation, sharing, security; government and private-sector applications; developing a 'paper GIS'

topics.name: Study of settlements and rural settlements
subtopics: Settlement, site and situation; rural vs urban settlements
Classification by size and complexity, pattern, function
Rural settlements: site/situation effects, patterns with advantages/disadvantages, functions, shapes (round, linear, T-shaped, crossroad), land use (farming, forestry, conservation)

topics.name: Rural settlement issues
subtopics: Rural-urban migration: push and pull factors; rural depopulation — causes, consequences, strategies, case study
Social justice issues: access to natural and human-made resources, limited investment, lack of infrastructure
Land reform: land tenure, redistribution, restitution
GIS: thematic data layering, manipulation and analysis; area and distance calculation

topics.name: Urban settlements
subtopics: Origin and development of urban settlement; urbanisation of the world population
Concepts: urbanisation, urban growth, urban expansion, urban sprawl, rate and level of urbanisation, counter-urbanisation
Site and situation; functional classification: central places, trade and transport towns (break-of-bulk, junction, gateway, gap), specialised towns
GIS: buffering, querying, data integration, statistical analysis

sba: Task 4: Controlled test (60 marks) OR mid-year exams (150 marks)

topics.name: Structure of the economy
subtopics: Economic sectors: primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary
Sector contributions to GNP and GDP; employment by sector
Use and interpretation of statistical and graphical information

topics.name: Agriculture
subtopics: Contribution of agriculture to the SA economy; small-scale vs large-scale farming
Main products for home and export markets
Maize case study: production areas, favouring/hindering factors, economic contribution
Food security: definitions, importance, influencing factors, improvement strategies, case studies

topics.name: Mining
subtopics: Contribution and significance of mining to SA's development
Platinum case study: location, favouring/hindering factors, economic contribution
Mapwork: identifying mining activity; grid referencing, map codes and symbols

topics.name: Secondary and tertiary sectors
subtopics: Contribution of the secondary sector
Types of industries: heavy/light, raw-material vs market orientated, footloose, ubiquitous, bridge (break-of-bulk)
Factors influencing industrial development: raw materials, labour, water, energy, transport, political intervention, competition, trade
Factors hindering industrial development (incl. over-concentration and pollution)

topics.name: SA industrial regions
subtopics: Four core regions: Gauteng (PWV), Durban-Pinetown, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage, South-Western Cape
Prescribed regions (Gauteng PWV and Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage): location factors, main activities, success factors and hindrances, economic and social impacts, case studies

topics.name: Revision: Settlement geography, Economic geography of SA, Map work skills and techniques

sba: Final NSC examination (Paper 1 and Paper 2, 150 marks, 3 hours each)

notes: Cognitive levels: lower order 25%, middle order 50%, higher order 25%
